# package pubsub

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub"
```

Package pubsub is the OPC UA PubSub runtime (Part 14): publishers that sample PublishedDataSets and send them as NetworkMessages, and subscribers that receive NetworkMessages and hand the DataSets to the application or write them to target variables.

#### Configuration {#hdr-Configuration}

The configuration is the standard PubSub configuration model of Part 14 §6.2, as generated in package ua: a [ua.PubSubConfigurationDataType](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#PubSubConfigurationDataType) holds the PublishedDataSets and the PubSubConnections, a connection holds WriterGroups and ReaderGroups, and those hold the DataSetWriters and DataSetReaders. Message and transport settings are the ExtensionObjects of the standard (UADPWriterGroupMessageDataType, BrokerWriterGroupTransportDataType, ...). The helpers of this package ([UDPConnection](#func-udpconnection), [WriterGroup](#func-writergroup), [PublishedDataItems](#func-publisheddataitems), [DataSetReader](#func-datasetreader), ...) fill those structures for the common cases; [Validate](#func-validate) checks a configuration and reports what is wrong.

DataSets are dynamic: the fields of a DataSet, their names and types, come from its DataSetMetaData and are versioned with its ConfigurationVersion.

#### Runtime {#hdr-Runtime}

[New](#func-new) creates a runtime for a configuration and [PubSub.Start](#func-pubsub-start) starts it. Every connection, group, writer, reader and published data set is a component with an id ([ComponentID](#type-componentid)) and, except the published data sets, a state machine (Part 14 §6.2.1): Disabled, Paused, PreOperational, Operational and Error. A component that is enabled runs when its parent is Operational and is Paused otherwise. Components can be added, removed, enabled and disabled while the runtime runs.

Publishers read the values of PublishedDataItems through a [DataSource](#type-datasource) and the events of PublishedEvents through an [EventSource](#type-eventsource). Subscribers deliver every received DataSet to a [DataSetHandler](#type-datasethandler) and write the fields of DataSetReaders with TargetVariables through a [TargetWriter](#type-targetwriter). The OPC UA server (package server, option WithPubSub) provides all three on its address space.

#### Message mappings, transports and security {#hdr-Message_mappings__transports_and_security}

NetworkMessages are encoded with the UADP mapping (package [github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/uadp](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/uadp)) or the JSON mapping (package [github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/jsonmsg](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/jsonmsg)), as selected by the message settings of the group, and sent over the transport registered for the scheme of the connection address (package [github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/transport](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/transport)). Secured groups get the keys of their SecurityGroup from a [security.KeySource](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/security#KeySource) given with [WithKeySource](#func-withkeysource) or [WithKeySourceLookup](#func-withkeysourcelookup).

#### Actions {#hdr-Actions}

PubSub Actions (Part 14 §6.2.11.2 in 1.05) call Action targets over PubSub. A Responder is a DataSetWriter of a PublishedAction ([PublishedActions](#func-publishedactions)) whose targets run the \[ActionHandler]s registered with [WithActionHandler](#func-withactionhandler) or [PubSub.SetActionHandler](#func-pubsub-setactionhandler); a Requestor calls them with [PubSub.CallAction](#func-pubsub-callaction). Both work over UDP and over MQTT and AMQP brokers, with the UADP (secured or not) and JSON mappings; [ActionOptions](#type-actionoptions) bound what a Responder accepts.

```go

```

```go

```

### func SetConnectionProperty

```go
func SetConnectionProperty(c *ua.PubSubConnectionDataType, name string, value any) *ua.PubSubConnectionDataType
```

SetConnectionProperty sets a connection property (a KeyValuePair of ConnectionProperties, key in namespace 0), replacing one of the same name. The MQTT transport understands the properties of Part 14 §7.3.4.4 (MqttVersion, "connection-Receive Maximum", ...; see package pubsub/transport/mqtt) and sends the others as MQTT 5.0 User Properties of the CONNECT. It panics if value cannot be a Variant.

### func SetJSONCompression

```go
func SetJSONCompression(c *ua.PubSubConnectionDataType, compression string) *ua.PubSubConnectionDataType
```

SetJSONCompression sets the compression of the JSON NetworkMessages a connection sends (the go-opcua connection property JsonCompression): "gzip" sends them gzip compressed with the Content Type application/json+gzip of Part 14 §7.3.4.9.1, "none" uncompressed. Part 14 defines the compressed content type for MQTT 5.0 only: Validate accepts the property on MQTT connections with the JSON mapping, and a connection that runs MQTT 3.1.1 (MqttVersion BestAvailable with a broker without 5.0) sends uncompressed. Subscribers decompress whatever compressed messages they receive, whatever this setting.

### func SetMQTTVersion

```go
func SetMQTTVersion(c *ua.PubSubConnectionDataType, version string) *ua.PubSubConnectionDataType
```

SetMQTTVersion selects the MQTT version of a broker connection with its MqttVersion connection property (Part 14 §7.3.4.4): MQTTVersion311 (the default of go-opcua), MQTTVersion5 or MQTTVersionBestAvailable (5.0 if the broker accepts it, else 3.1.1). With MQTT 5.0 the messages carry their content type and message type.

## Types

### type ActionHandler

```go
type ActionHandler func(ctx context.Context, inputs []*ua.Variant) ([]*ua.Variant, ua.StatusCode)
```

ActionHandler executes an Action target. inputs are the fields of the request, in the order of the request DataSetMetaData of the PublishedAction (when it has fields, their number and built-in types are checked before the handler runs). It returns the output fields, in the order of the response DataSetMetaData (the DataSetMetaData of the PublishedDataSet), and the result: the outputs of a Bad result are not sent.

ctx ends with the TimeoutHint of the request (at most ActionOptions.MaxTimeout), when the runtime or the writer stops; a handler must return then, since [PubSub.Close](#func-pubsub-close) waits for it (and so a handler must not call Close itself). [ActionInvocationFrom](#func-actioninvocationfrom) tells which request it serves. A panic is recovered and answered with Bad\_InternalError.

### type ActionTarget

```go
type ActionTarget struct {
	// Connection is the name of the connection of this runtime the
	// request is sent on. It needs a PublisherId: it is the RequestorId.
	// Its transport profile selects the message mapping.
	Connection string
	// PublisherID (a byte, uint16, uint32, uint64, string or a
	// message.PublisherID), DataSetWriterID and ActionTargetID address the
	// Action target of the Responder.
	PublisherID     any
	DataSetWriterID uint16
	ActionTargetID  uint16
	// RequestAddress is where the request is sent: the QueueName of the
	// Responder's writer group on a broker (required, see
	// [ActionRequestTopic]); on a datagram transport an address such as
	// opc.udp://host:port, empty for the address of the connection.
	RequestAddress string
	// ResponseAddress is where the Responder sends its responses. Empty
	// selects on a broker the action-response topic corresponding to the
	// RequestAddress, on a datagram transport the address of the
	// connection (sent along when RequestAddress is another one). The
	// connection subscribes to it for the call.
	ResponseAddress string
	// SecurityMode and SecurityGroupID secure the UADP messages of the
	// call; the Responder answers with the security of its writer group.
	SecurityMode    ua.MessageSecurityMode
	SecurityGroupID string
	// RequestMetaData names the input fields for the JSON mapping and
	// ResponseMetaData describes the outputs (field order of JSON
	// messages, RawData fields). Without them inputs are named "Field0",
	// "Field1", ... (the default names of the Responder's DataSetMetaData)
	// and outputs are taken in the order received.
	RequestMetaData  *ua.DataSetMetaDataType
	ResponseMetaData *ua.DataSetMetaDataType
	// Timeout is the TimeoutHint of the request and how long CallAction
	// waits for the Done response. Zero uses the deadline of the context
	// or ActionOptions.DefaultTimeout.
	Timeout time.Duration
	// MetaDataAddress is, on a broker, where the Responder announces the
	// ActionMetaData of the writer for [PubSub.DiscoverAction]: the
	// MetaDataQueueName of the writer (see [ActionMetaDataTopic]).
	MetaDataAddress string
	// ResendInterval, if positive, is the PublishingInterval of the
	// Responder on a non-reliable (datagram) transport: the request is
	// resent while no response arrives within it, and the Idle
	// acknowledgement until the Responder confirms it (Part 14 Table 83).
	ResendInterval time.Duration
	// MaxNetworkMessageSize bounds the request messages: a larger UADP
	// request is sent as chunks (Part 14 §7.2.4.4.4), a larger JSON request
	// fails. 0 takes the limit of the transport. The Responder chunks its
	// responses after the MaxNetworkMessageSize of its writer group.
	MaxNetworkMessageSize uint32
}
```

ActionTarget addresses an Action target of a Responder for [PubSub.CallAction](#func-pubsub-callaction).

### type ComponentID

```go
type ComponentID uint32
```

ComponentID identifies a component of a PubSub runtime: a connection, a group, a writer, a reader or a published data set. Ids are never reused within a runtime. Root is the runtime itself.

```go
const Root ComponentID = 0
```

Root is the id of the runtime itself (the PublishSubscribe object) for [PubSub.Enable](#func-pubsub-enable), [PubSub.Disable](#func-pubsub-disable), [PubSub.State](#func-pubsub-state) and [PubSub.Status](#func-pubsub-status).

### type Counters

```go
type Counters struct {
	// NetworkMessagesSent and NetworkMessagesReceived count NetworkMessages,
	// BytesSent and BytesReceived their encoded size.
	NetworkMessagesSent     uint64
	NetworkMessagesReceived uint64
	BytesSent               uint64
	BytesReceived           uint64
	// DataSetMessagesSent and DataSetMessagesReceived count DataSetMessages
	// with data (key frames, delta frames, events); keep-alive messages are
	// counted separately.
	DataSetMessagesSent     uint64
	DataSetMessagesReceived uint64
	KeepAlivesSent          uint64
	KeepAlivesReceived      uint64
	// MetaDataSent and MetaDataReceived count DataSetMetaData messages.
	MetaDataSent     uint64
	MetaDataReceived uint64
	// EncodeErrors, SendErrors and DecodeErrors count failures of the codecs
	// and the transport.
	EncodeErrors uint64
	SendErrors   uint64
	DecodeErrors uint64
	// SequenceDiscards counts DataSetMessages discarded as duplicates, as
	// older than the last one received or as invalid (a quarter or more of
	// the number space away, Part 14 §7.2.3); SequenceResyncs counts
	// writers the reader resynchronised to a lower sequence number after
	// their sequence record expired (no message for two
	// MessageReceiveTimeouts).
	SequenceDiscards uint64
	SequenceResyncs  uint64
	// VersionMismatches counts DataSetMessages discarded because their
	// MetaData version does not match the reader's.
	VersionMismatches uint64
	// Timeouts counts MessageReceiveTimeouts of readers.
	Timeouts uint64
	// TargetWriteErrors counts failed writes to target variables.
	TargetWriteErrors uint64
	// StateChanges counts state transitions.
	StateChanges uint64
	// Panics counts panics the runtime recovered from: in an application
	// callback (DataSetHandler, DataSource, TargetWriter, event handler) or
	// while decoding a received message. They are logged with their stack.
	Panics uint64

	// ChunksSent and ChunksReceived count UADP chunk NetworkMessages
	// (Part 14 §7.2.4.4.4); they are NetworkMessages as well.
	// ChunkedMessagesReceived counts the messages reassembled from them.
	// ChunksDiscarded counts received chunks the reassembly rejected
	// (outside their message, duplicate or overlapping, beyond the memory
	// limits) or dropped with an incomplete message (timeout, eviction).
	ChunksSent              uint64
	ChunksReceived          uint64
	ChunkedMessagesReceived uint64
	ChunksDiscarded         uint64
	// NonceSequenceDiscards counts secured UADP NetworkMessages (chunks
	// included) ignored because the sequence number of their MessageNonce
	// is not newer than the last one processed for their sender and
	// SecurityTokenId (Part 14 §7.2.4.4.3.2, §7.2.3): repeated or late
	// copies.
	NonceSequenceDiscards uint64
	// DiscoveryRequestsSent and DiscoveryRequestsReceived count UADP
	// discovery probes (Part 14 §7.2.4.6.12); DiscoveryRequestsIgnored
	// counts received probes that were not answered: not for this
	// publisher, duplicates, or beyond the rate limit.
	// DiscoveryResponsesSent counts the announcements sent in answer to
	// probes or cyclically, DiscoveryResponsesReceived the announcements
	// received.
	DiscoveryRequestsSent      uint64
	DiscoveryRequestsReceived  uint64
	DiscoveryRequestsIgnored   uint64
	DiscoveryResponsesSent     uint64
	DiscoveryResponsesReceived uint64

	// PubSub Actions (Part 14 §6.2.11.2 in 1.05). The Requestor counts
	// the ActionRequestsSent (every request message, resends and Idle
	// acknowledgements included), the ActionResponsesReceived for its
	// calls and the ActionTimeouts of calls that got no Done response in
	// time. The Responder counts the ActionRequestsReceived for its
	// Action writers, the ActionResponsesSent, and the
	// ActionRequestsRejected: requests for an unknown writer or Action
	// target, without the security the writer group requires, beyond the
	// rate or concurrency limits, or whose response could not be
	// addressed. Duplicates of a running or completed request are counted
	// as received but not executed again.
	ActionRequestsSent      uint64
	ActionRequestsReceived  uint64
	ActionRequestsRejected  uint64
	ActionResponsesSent     uint64
	ActionResponsesReceived uint64
	ActionTimeouts          uint64
}
```

Counters are the diagnostic counters of a component. The counters of a group include those of its writers or readers, the counters of a connection those of its groups.

### type DataSetHandler

```go
type DataSetHandler func(ds *ReceivedDataSet)
```

DataSetHandler receives the DataSets of all DataSetReaders. It is called outside the runtime's lock, in the order the messages were received on a connection, and must not block for long. It runs on the receiving goroutine of the transport, which [PubSub.Close](#func-pubsub-close) waits for: a handler must not call Close (it may start it in a goroutine of its own). Nor may it wait for [PubSub.CallAction](#func-pubsub-callaction): the response would arrive on the goroutine the handler blocks.

### type DataSource

```go
type DataSource interface {
	ReadPublishedData(ctx context.Context, vars []*ua.PublishedVariableDataType) []*ua.DataValue
}
```

DataSource reads the values of PublishedDataItems for the publisher.

ReadPublishedData returns one DataValue per variable, in order. It honours the AttributeId and the IndexRange of the PublishedVariableDataType; the runtime applies the SubstituteValue to Bad values itself. A missing value is reported with a Bad status, not by leaving the slot nil.

### type DataSourceFunc

```go
type DataSourceFunc func(ctx context.Context, vars []*ua.PublishedVariableDataType) []*ua.DataValue
```

DataSourceFunc adapts a function to a [DataSource](#type-datasource).

#### func (DataSourceFunc) ReadPublishedData

```go
func (f DataSourceFunc) ReadPublishedData(ctx context.Context, vars []*ua.PublishedVariableDataType) []*ua.DataValue
```

ReadPublishedData calls f.

### type Diagnostics

```go
type Diagnostics struct {
	ComponentInfo
	// Level is the DiagnosticsLevel of the object.
	Level ua.DiagnosticsLevel
	// TotalInformation and TotalError are the sums of the active counters
	// classified Information and Error; TotalInformationFirstChange and
	// TotalErrorFirstChange the earliest TimeFirstChange among them.
	TotalInformation            uint32
	TotalError                  uint32
	TotalInformationFirstChange time.Time
	TotalErrorFirstChange       time.Time
	// SubError reports whether the diagnostics object of a child (the
	// connections of the runtime, the groups of a connection, the
	// writers or readers of a group) has a TotalError above 0.
	SubError bool
	// Counters are the counters of the component kind, in the order of

}
```

Diagnostics is the diagnostics object of a component (Part 14 §9.1.11).


### type DiagnosticsCounter

```go
type DiagnosticsCounter struct {
	ID DiagnosticsCounterID
	// Value is the count since the last reset; it stops at the largest
	// UInt32.
	Value uint32
	// Active reports whether the counter counts: its Level is within the
	// DiagnosticsLevel of the object. An inactive counter keeps its value
	// and is set to 0 when it becomes active again.
	Active         bool
	Classification ua.PubSubDiagnosticsCounterClassification
	Level          ua.DiagnosticsLevel
	// TimeFirstChange is when the value went from 0 to 1; zero while the
	// value is 0.
	TimeFirstChange time.Time
}
```

DiagnosticsCounter is the value of a diagnostics counter (PubSubDiagnosticsCounterType, Part 14 §9.1.11.5).

### type DiagnosticsCounterID

```go
type DiagnosticsCounterID uint8
```

DiagnosticsCounterID identifies a counter of the PubSub diagnostics objects (Part 14 §9.1.11): the state counters every component has (PubSubDiagnosticsType, §9.1.11.2) and the counters of the subtypes for writer groups, reader groups, writers and readers (§9.1.11.9 to §9.1.11.12). Its String is the BrowseName of the counter.

```go
const (
	// CounterStateError counts transitions to Error (§9.1.11.2).
	CounterStateError DiagnosticsCounterID = iota
	// CounterStateOperationalByMethod counts transitions to Operational
	// caused by the Enable method of the component.
	CounterStateOperationalByMethod
	// CounterStateOperationalByParent counts transitions to Operational
	// because the parent became Operational.
	CounterStateOperationalByParent
	// CounterStateOperationalFromError counts transitions from Error to
	// Operational.
	CounterStateOperationalFromError
	// CounterStatePausedByParent counts transitions to Paused because the
	// parent is Paused or Disabled.
	CounterStatePausedByParent
	// CounterStateDisabledByMethod counts transitions to Disabled caused
	// by the Disable method of the component.
	CounterStateDisabledByMethod
	// CounterSentNetworkMessages counts the NetworkMessages a writer group
	// sent (§9.1.11.9).
	CounterSentNetworkMessages
	// CounterFailedTransmissions counts the NetworkMessages of a writer
	// group that could not be encoded or sent.
	CounterFailedTransmissions
	// CounterEncryptionErrors counts the NetworkMessages of a writer group
	// that could not be signed or encrypted.
	CounterEncryptionErrors
	// CounterReceivedNetworkMessages counts the NetworkMessages a reader
	// group received and processed (§9.1.11.10).
	CounterReceivedNetworkMessages
	// CounterReceivedInvalidNetworkMessages counts received NetworkMessages
	// for a reader group that could not be decoded.
	CounterReceivedInvalidNetworkMessages
	// CounterDecryptionErrors counts received NetworkMessages that failed
	// the security checks (signature, decryption, keys, security mode) of
	// a reader group or a reader.
	CounterDecryptionErrors
	// CounterFailedDataSetMessages counts the DataSetMessages of a writer
	// that could not be encoded or sent (§9.1.11.11), and the received
	// DataSetMessages a reader could not process: a MajorVersion that
	// does not match its DataSetMetaData or fields it cannot place
	// (§9.1.11.12).
	CounterFailedDataSetMessages
)
```

Diagnostics counters.

DiagnosticsCountersOf returns the counters of the diagnostics object of a component kind, in the order of the specification. Published data sets have no diagnostics object.

Classification is the classification of a counter: Error for the counters of failures, Information for the others (Part 14 §9.1.11.6).

Level is the DiagnosticsLevel a counter belongs to (Part 14 §9.1.11.4): the counter is active while the DiagnosticsLevel of its object is at least this level. The counters of the message security and of invalid messages are Advanced, the others Basic.

```go
type DiagnosticsLiveValues struct {
	// ConfiguredDataSetWriters and OperationalDataSetWriters count the
	// writers of the runtime (PublishSubscribe) or of a writer group, all
	// and those that are Operational.
	ConfiguredDataSetWriters  uint16
	OperationalDataSetWriters uint16
	// ConfiguredDataSetReaders and OperationalDataSetReaders count the
	// readers of the runtime or of a reader group.
	ConfiguredDataSetReaders  uint16
	OperationalDataSetReaders uint16

	ResolvedAddress string

	// DataSetMetaData of a writer or a reader.

	MinorVersion uint32

}
```

DiagnosticsLiveValues are the LiveValues of a diagnostics object. Which of them a component kind has, and at which DiagnosticsLevel, is defined by Part 14 §9.1.11.7 to §9.1.11.12; the others are zero.

### type DiscoveryOptions

```go
type DiscoveryOptions struct {
	// Disabled turns discovery off: no probes are sent or answered and no
	// cyclic announcements are sent.
	Disabled bool
	// MinInterval is the least time between two announcements of the same
	// kind and writer (default 500 ms, the minimum of Part 14
	// §7.2.4.6.12.2): probes for it in between are ignored.
	MinInterval time.Duration
	// Rate and Burst bound the announcements a connection sends in answer
	// to probes, all kinds and writers together (default 20 per second,
	// bursts of 20): probes cannot make a publisher flood the network.
	Rate  float64
	Burst int
	// MaxProbeInterval bounds the interval between the probes of a
	// subscriber, which doubles from 500 ms while the announcement is
	// missing (default 8 seconds).
	MaxProbeInterval time.Duration
	// Layout is the byte layout of the probes the subscriber sends: the
	// spec's (default) or that of the OPC Foundation .NET stack. Probes
	// are answered in the layout they came in.
	Layout message.DiscoveryLayout
	// Endpoints returns the server endpoints of the publisher for
	// PublisherEndpoints probes; without it they are answered with
	// Bad_NotSupported.
	Endpoints func() []*ua.EndpointDescription
	// Application returns the ApplicationDescription of the publisher, and
	// Capabilities are its capabilities, for FindApplications probes;
	// without it they are answered with the state of the runtime.
	Application  func() *ua.ApplicationDescription
	Capabilities []string
}
```

DiscoveryOptions control the UADP discovery of datagram connections (Part 14 §7.2.4.6): the probes a subscriber sends for DataSetMetaData it does not have, and the announcements a publisher sends in answer to probes. Zero fields select the defaults.

### type Option


Option configures a runtime.

#### func WithActionHandler


WithActionHandler registers the handler of the Action target actionTargetID of the PublishedAction dataSetName (Responder). A target without handler is answered with Bad\_NotImplemented.


WithActionMethodCaller sets how the targets of PublishedActionMethods call their Methods. A handler registered for a target with [WithActionHandler](#func-withactionhandler) takes precedence; a target with neither is answered with Bad\_NotImplemented.

```go

```

WithActionOptions sets the limits of the PubSub Actions.

#### func WithChunkReassembly

```go

```

WithChunkReassembly sets the limits of the reassembly of chunked UADP NetworkMessages: the largest message, the memory of the incomplete messages of each connection, overall and per PublisherId, and how long an incomplete message waits for its chunks. Zero fields keep the defaults of [uadp.ReassemblerOptions](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/uadp#ReassemblerOptions).

#### func WithDataSetHandler

```go

```

WithDataSetHandler adds a handler for the DataSets received by all DataSetReaders.

#### func WithDataSource

```go

```

WithDataSource sets the source of the values of PublishedDataItems.

#### func WithDiagnosticsLevel

```go

```

WithDiagnosticsLevel sets the DiagnosticsLevel the diagnostics objects of the components start with. The default is Basic.

#### func WithDiscovery

```go
func WithDiscovery(o DiscoveryOptions) Option
```

WithDiscovery sets the options of the UADP discovery.

#### func WithEventHandler

```go
func WithEventHandler(h func(Event)) Option
```

WithEventHandler adds a handler for the events of the runtime: components added and removed, and state changes. Handlers run on the goroutine that made the change, which is a goroutine of the runtime for the state changes of a connection and its readers: they must not block for long, call [PubSub.Close](#func-pubsub-close) or wait for [PubSub.CallAction](#func-pubsub-callaction) (start those in a goroutine of their own).

#### func WithEventSource

```go
func WithEventSource(es EventSource) Option
```

WithEventSource sets the source of the events of PublishedEvents.

#### func WithJSONDecompressionLimit

```go
func WithJSONDecompressionLimit(n int) Option
```

WithJSONDecompressionLimit sets the largest JSON NetworkMessage a subscriber decompresses from a gzip compressed message (Part 14 §7.3.4.9.1); larger ones are decode errors. The default is DefaultJSONDecompressionLimit.

#### func WithKeySource

```go
func WithKeySource(securityGroupID string, ks security.KeySource) Option
```

WithKeySource sets the keys of a SecurityGroup: groups with the SecurityGroupId secure their messages with them. ks is typically a static key ring or a client of a Security Key Service.

#### func WithKeySourceLookup

```go
func WithKeySourceLookup(l KeySourceLookup) Option
```

WithKeySourceLookup adds a lookup for the keys of SecurityGroups that were not set with [WithKeySource](#func-withkeysource) or [PubSub.SetKeySource](#func-pubsub-setkeysource). Lookups are asked in the order they were added.

#### func WithLogger

```go
func WithLogger(l *slog.Logger) Option
```

WithLogger sets the logger. The default discards log output.

#### func WithNonceSequencePerToken

```go
func WithNonceSequencePerToken(on bool) Option
```

WithNonceSequencePerToken makes the receivers keep the last MessageNonce sequence number of a secured publisher (Part 14 §7.2.4.4.3.2) for as long as its SecurityTokenId is in the KeySource, instead of discarding it, as §7.2.3 does with sequence records, after two MessageReceiveTimeouts of the readers without a message. A copy of an earlier message is then ignored also after the publisher was silent; a publisher that restarts and secures its messages with the same token, counting from 1 again, is ignored until it uses the next token. The sequence numbers of ActionRequests and ActionResponses are always kept per token.

#### func WithRetryInterval

```go
func WithRetryInterval(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithRetryInterval sets how long a connection whose transport failed to open (state Error) waits before it tries again. The default is 5 seconds.

#### func WithTargetWriter

```go
func WithTargetWriter(tw TargetWriter) Option
```

WithTargetWriter sets the writer of TargetVariables (and, if it implements [MirrorWriter](#type-mirrorwriter), of SubscribedDataSetMirrors).

#### func WithTransportConfig

```go

```

WithTransportConfig adds a hook that completes the transport configuration of a connection before it is opened: MQTT credentials, a TLS configuration, multicast settings.

### type PubSub

```go
type PubSub struct {

	// pending are the callbacks (events, handlers, target writes, event
	// subscriptions) collected under mu; unlock runs them after releasing
	// it, in order.

	// reqSeq numbers the RequestIds of CallAction (guarded by mu);
	// actNonces the secured action requests, which actMu sends in the
	// order of their nonces.

	// actSeq numbers the chunked action messages (their
	// MessageSequenceNumber).

}
```

PubSub is a PubSub runtime: the publishers and subscribers of one configuration. Create it with [New](#func-new) and run it with [PubSub.Start](#func-pubsub-start).

All methods are safe for concurrent use.

#### func New

```go
func New(cfg *ua.PubSubConfigurationDataType, opts ...Option) (*PubSub, error)
```

New creates a runtime for a configuration. cfg may be nil for an empty, enabled runtime to which components are added later. The configuration is copied; later changes to cfg have no effect.

AddConnection adds a PubSubConnection with its groups, writers and readers. It returns the id of the connection.

```go
func (p *PubSub) AddDataSetWriter(group ComponentID, cfg *ua.DataSetWriterDataType) (ComponentID, error)
```

AddDataSetWriter adds a DataSetWriter to a WriterGroup. Its DataSetName must name an existing PublishedDataSet; an empty DataSetName makes a writer that sends only keep-alive messages.

#### func (PubSub) AddPublishedDataSet

```go
func (p *PubSub) AddPublishedDataSet(cfg *ua.PublishedDataSetDataType) (ComponentID, error)
```

AddPublishedDataSet adds a PublishedDataSet. Without DataSetMetaData, or with one without fields, the metadata is derived from the published variables (through the [FieldMetaDataResolver](#type-fieldmetadataresolver) of the DataSource if it has one). A ConfigurationVersion of 0 is set to the current VersionTime.

#### func (PubSub) AddReaderGroup

```go
func (p *PubSub) AddReaderGroup(conn ComponentID, cfg *ua.ReaderGroupDataType) (ComponentID, error)
```

AddReaderGroup adds a ReaderGroup (with its DataSetReaders) to a connection.

#### func (PubSub) AddWriterGroup

```go
func (p *PubSub) AddWriterGroup(conn ComponentID, cfg *ua.WriterGroupDataType) (ComponentID, error)
```

AddWriterGroup adds a WriterGroup (with its DataSetWriters) to a connection.

#### func (PubSub) CallAction

```go
func (p *PubSub) CallAction(ctx context.Context, t ActionTarget, inputs []*ua.Variant) (*ActionResult, error)
```

CallAction calls an Action target of a Responder (the Requestor of Part 14 §6.2.11.2 in 1.05): it sends the request with the inputs on the connection t.Connection and waits for the Done response, which it acknowledges. It returns the result of the Action; an error is returned when the call could not be made or completed: an invalid target, a connection that is not running, ErrActionTimeout (Bad\_Timeout) when no Done response came in time, the error of ctx, or Bad\_NotConnected when the connection stopped meanwhile.

The connection must be running: CallAction waits until its transport is open and subscribed to the response address, within the timeout.

#### func (PubSub) Close

```go
func (p *PubSub) Close() error
```

Close stops the runtime and waits for its goroutines. It closes all transports. Close is idempotent; the runtime cannot be started again.

The callbacks of the runtime (DataSetHandler, TargetWriter, event handlers, DataSource) run on its goroutines: calling Close from one of them deadlocks. Start it in a goroutine of its own instead.


Component returns the description of a component.


Components lists the components of the runtime: connections, each followed by its writer groups with their writers and its reader groups with their readers, then the published data sets.

Configuration returns the current configuration of the runtime, including the components added at run time and the DataSetMetaData readers learned from metadata messages.


#### func (PubSub) Disable

```go
func (p *PubSub) Disable(id ComponentID) error
```

Disable disables a component (or, with Root, the runtime). It fails with Bad\_InvalidState if the component is already Disabled.

#### func (PubSub) DiscoverAction

```go
func (p *PubSub) DiscoverAction(ctx context.Context, t ActionTarget) (*ActionMetaData, error)
```

DiscoverAction returns the ActionMetaData of the Action writer of a Responder addressed by t (Connection, PublisherID, DataSetWriterID and, for UADP, SecurityMode and SecurityGroupID). On a broker it is read from the retained message on t.MetaDataAddress (see [ActionMetaDataTopic](#func-actionmetadatatopic)); on a datagram transport it is probed for on the discovery channel of the connection (its DiscoveryAddress or shared connection address), where the Responder answers. It waits up to t.Timeout (or the deadline of ctx, or ActionOptions.DefaultTimeout) and fails with Bad\_Timeout. Apply the result to the target for [PubSub.CallAction](#func-pubsub-callaction).

#### func (PubSub) Enable

```go
func (p *PubSub) Enable(id ComponentID) error
```

Enable enables a component (or, with Root, the runtime). Like the Enable method of the PubSubStatusType it fails with Bad\_InvalidState if the component is not Disabled.

```go

```

KeySource returns the keys of a SecurityGroup, nil if none are known.

#### func (PubSub) Lookup


#### func (PubSub) Ready

```go
func (p *PubSub) Ready(ctx context.Context) error
```

Ready waits until every running connection has opened its transport and made its first subscriptions: those of its readers, its discovery listener and its Action requests and responses. A datagram or broker message sent to the runtime after Ready reaches it; one sent before may be lost. A subscription that failed is retried in the background and shows in the Status of the connection; Ready does not wait for the retry.

Ready waits as long as a transport does not open (a broker that is not reachable): bound it with ctx. It returns an error if the runtime is not running or stops while waiting, or ctx ends.


ResetDiagnostics sets the counters of the diagnostics object of a component (or, with Root, of the runtime) back to 0 (the Reset method, Part 14 §9.1.11.3). It does not reset the counters of the children, nor the [Counters](#type-counters) of [PubSub.Status](#func-pubsub-status).



#### func (PubSub) SetKeySource

```go

```

SetKeySource sets (or, with nil, removes) the keys of a SecurityGroup at run time, for example when a Security Key Service pushes new keys.

#### func (PubSub) Start

```go
func (p *PubSub) Start(ctx context.Context) error
```

Start starts the runtime: connections open their transports, writer groups publish and readers subscribe. Cancelling ctx stops the runtime again (all components become Paused) until the next Start. Start on a running runtime does nothing; Start after Close returns ErrClosed.

The transports open in the background: Start returns before the readers can receive. [PubSub.Ready](#func-pubsub-ready) waits for that.

### type PublishedField

```go
type PublishedField struct {
	Field
	// NodeID is the published variable; its Value attribute is published.
	NodeID *ua.NodeID
	// IndexRange publishes a part of an array value.
	IndexRange string
	// Substitute, if not nil, is published with the status
	// Uncertain_SubstituteValue when the value is Bad.
	Substitute any
}
```

PublishedField is a published variable.

#### func Var

```go
func Var(name string, nodeID *ua.NodeID, typ ua.TypeID) PublishedField
```

Var returns a PublishedField.

### type ReceivedDataSet

```go
type ReceivedDataSet struct {
	// Reader is the id of the DataSetReader, ReaderName its name.
	Reader     ComponentID
	ReaderName string

	PublisherID     message.PublisherID
	WriterGroupID   uint16
	DataSetWriterID uint16
	// SequenceNumber of the DataSetMessage (0 if the message had none).
	SequenceNumber uint32
	// Timestamp of the DataSetMessage, or of the NetworkMessage if the
	// DataSetMessage had none, or the reception time.
	Timestamp time.Time
	// Status of the DataSetMessage.
	Status ua.StatusCode
	// MessageType is KeyFrame, DeltaFrame or Event.
	MessageType message.DataSetMessageType
	// MetaDataVersion is the ConfigurationVersion of the DataSetMetaData
	// the message was decoded with.
	MetaDataVersion ua.ConfigurationVersionDataType

	// Fields are all fields of the DataSet in DataSetMetaData order. A
	// delta frame is merged onto the last key frame, so Fields always holds
	// the latest value of every field. Events carry their own fields.
	Fields []ReceivedField
	// Changed are the indexes of the fields this message carried.
	Changed []int
	// Complete reports whether every field has a value: a key frame (or an
	// event) was received.
	Complete bool
}
```

ReceivedDataSet is a DataSet received by a DataSetReader, given to the [DataSetHandler](#type-datasethandler).

#### func (ReceivedDataSet) Field

```go
func (d *ReceivedDataSet) Field(name string) *ua.DataValue
```

Field returns the value of the field with the given name, or nil.

### type ReceivedField

```go
type ReceivedField struct {
	// Index is the position of the field in the DataSetMetaData.
	Index int
	// Name is the field name from the DataSetMetaData (or the message).
	Name string
	// Value is the last value received for the field; nil if no value was
	// received yet (delta frames before the first key frame).
	Value *ua.DataValue
}
```

ReceivedField is one field of a received DataSet.

### type Status

```go
type Status struct {
	ComponentInfo
	// LastError is the last error of the component (the reason of the
	// Error state, or the last send or decode failure), nil if none.
	LastError error
	// Counters of the component and, aggregated, of its children.
	Counters Counters
}
```

Status is the state and the diagnostics of a component.

### type TargetWrite

```go
type TargetWrite struct {
	// Reader is the id of the DataSetReader the write is for.
	Reader ComponentID
	// Target is the target variable: TargetNodeId, AttributeId and
	// WriteIndexRange. The ReceiverIndexRange is already applied to Value.
	Target *ua.FieldTargetDataType
	// Value is the value to write, with its status and timestamps.
	Value *ua.DataValue
}
```

TargetWrite is one write of a received field to a target variable.

### type TargetWriter

```go
type TargetWriter interface {
	WriteTargets(ctx context.Context, writes []TargetWrite) []error
}
```

TargetWriter writes the fields of DataSetReaders configured with TargetVariables to their target variables. It returns one error (nil for success) per write.

### type TargetWriterFunc

```go
type TargetWriterFunc func(ctx context.Context, writes []TargetWrite) []error
```

TargetWriterFunc adapts a function to a [TargetWriter](#type-targetwriter).


WriteTargets calls f.
